newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Philadelphia Fed releases Q3 '96 survey.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Philadelphia Fed releases Q3 '96 survey.

text.p: The following was released by the Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank.
NEW YORK, Aug 27 - Economic growth over the second half of 1996 will decelerate from the first half's rapid pace, according to 42 forecasters surveyed by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
The forecasters expect real GDP to grow at an annual rate of 2.45 percent in the second half, down from the annual rate of 3.1 percent registered in the first half.
Further deceleration is expected over the first three quarters of 1997, when real GDP will grow at an annual rate of 1.9 percent.
On a year-over-year basis, real GDP will expand at an annual rate of 2.3 percent in 1996 and 2.2 percent in 1997.
Reduced price pressure will accompany the second-half slowdown.
Inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index, will average 2.8 percent over the second half of 1996, down from an annual rate of 3.5 percent in the first half of the year.
Inflation will average 3.2 percent for the year and fall to 3.0 percent in 1997.
The forecasters see the unemployment rate holding steady at 5.4 percent through the first quarter of 1997 and drifting upward to 5.6 percent by the third quarter.

The current outlook does not foresee major changes in interest rates. Short-term interest rates, as measured by the rate on three-month Treasury bills, will rise to 5.3 percent in the first half of 1997 and fall back toward current levels over the second half.
The rate on 10-year Treasury bonds will hold steady at 6.7 percent through the first quarter of 1997 and fall over the remainder of the year.

Forecasters See Reduced Chance of a Negative Quarter
The slowdown in real GDP growth over the next five quarters does not raise the risk of a negative quarter compared with the risk assigned in last quarter's survey.

Currently, the forecasters are assigning a 7 percent chance to a negative third quarter, down from 10 percent in last quarter's survey. The following table compares the probabilities from the current survey with those from three months ago:

Forecasters Expect No Change in Long-Term Inflation

The forecasters continue to expect inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index, to average 3.0 percent over the next 10 years, marking the third consecutive survey in which long-term expectations are unchanged. The middle range of forecasts is 2.80 to 3.44 percent.
Forecasters Peg the Natural Rate at 5.65 Percent

This survey marks the second consecutive third-quarter survey in which we asked our forecasters about their use of the natural rate of unemployment-- that rate of unemployment that occurs when the economy reaches equilibrium. Of those responding to our inquiry (39 forecasters), 62 percent indicate that they use the natural-rate concept in formulating their forecasts, up from 57 percent in 1995. These forecasters estimate that the natural rate is currently 5.65 percent, down from 5.75 percent in the 1995 survey. The middle range of estimates is 5.48 to 5.80 percent.

The Philadelphia Fed's Survey of Professional Forecasters was formerly conducted by the American Statistical Association (ASA) and the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) and was known as the ASA/NBER survey. The survey, which began in 1968, is conducted each quarter. The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, in cooperation with the NBER, assumed responsibility for the survey in June 1990.

For further information about the Survey of Professional Forecasters, contact: Dean Croushore, Assistant Vice President and Economist, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Ten Independence Mall, Philadelphia, PA 19106 215-574-3809.
To subscribe to the survey, contact the Research Department's Publications Desk at 215-574-6428. This three-page writeup contains partial results of the survey.
